label: Day 2 — What a protocol violation actually looks like
tweets: Yesterday: broken *sequences* are the blind spot of AI code. Today: three concrete shapes. 🧵

1/3 — MISSING STEP across functions.

register() calls storeUser(u, p), but hashPassword() — two files away — is never invoked on this path → plaintext passwords in the DB.

A linter sees two valid calls. Progmune models the rule: storeUser requires state PASSWORD_HASHED.

2/3 — WRONG ORDER. Lifecycle is open→write→close. AI writes:

conn = open()
conn.close()
conn.query()  ← use-after-close

close() *invalidates* the open state; query() requires it. A state machine catches this instantly. Regex on lines? No.

3/3 NEVER RELEASED. AI opens a resource in one helper; the close() never runs.
Per-function analyzers miss it — acquire here, release elsewhere. Progmune tracks acquire→release across calls, incl. end-of-seq leaks.
Why SAST/SCA miss these → tomorrow. #AISecurity #infosec
